sheet_from: Data/World3/Tile*.OZJ, from MuMain, decoded under a dv_ prefix. The prefix is load-bearing as nr_ and cs_ are: assets/textures is one flat pool, and nine of these fourteen names are Lorencia's too, so unprefixed the snowfield would have been answered by the town's lawn. docs/devias-ground.md section 2.
slot_note: All fourteen slots are painted, where Lorencia and Noria each paint nine: Devias is a town of interiors, and slots 10-13 are the church's and the halls' floors. TileRock01 is 0.0% as a base and is the ice painted over the moat's water as an overlay (mean alpha 204).
material_note: Read off the art, which lies here in a snowy direction. Both TileGrass sheets are snow, a creased snowfield and a smoother bright one, 81.4% of the map between them; neither takes grass, because the grass pass sows its sward on every slot whose recipe is grass. TileWood01 is not wood but mottled blue rime and takes snow; TileRock01 is packed blue ice and takes ice. TileGround01 is grey trodden gravel, the road, and takes sand, the shallowest ground. TileGround02 is dark floorboards, the interiors, and takes plank. TileGround03 is crazy paving with snow packed deep in the joints and takes cobble for the channel. TileRock02 and 03 are pitted slabs and take flagstone. TileRock04 and 06 are polished marble, grey with an inlay and black with gold veins, and take the new marble; TileRock05 and 07 are a red carpet and a bordered rug and take cloth.
tile_note: Slots 10-13 are patterned floors, one decorated piece per repeat, laid at MU's own reach. Water is 3.9% and nearly all of it is the moat under the ice; MU scrolls it once every twenty seconds under an overlay that does not move.
